# T-050 The slam grows with each cut

**Block:** session 5 · **Status:** doing

## Goal

The author's request (Sat 14 Nov 15:45): the Publisher's slam becomes a pattern that grows with each cut. Before the
first cut, one circle on the hero as now. After the first cut, 3 circles: one around him (no standing close), one
exactly on the hero, one behind the hero that cuts off the way back. From the second cut to the end, 5: the same plus
two more beside the hero. Answers in chat: 1-3-5-5-5; the circle on the hero stays 300 cm, the others are smaller; they
land one after another, 0.2 s apart, from him outwards; a landed cash stack is never covered; the dash still protects.

## Scope

- Simulation, `JamSlamRules`: the circle count by the cuts done, the seeded placement, and the nearest spot the hero
  can walk to in time (walking only: the dash may be stolen). A cutter that would shut every way out is left out; a
  circle over a cash stack is pushed off it. Numbers in `[JamBalance]`.
- The boss puts the whole pattern down in one slam and stands until the last circle lands plus his pause.
- The bot walks to the safe spot while circles are on the floor (the old rule left the first circle only).
- View and sound unchanged: each circle fills on its own clock, each landing flashes, thuds and shakes.

## Test seam

`Jam.Slam.TheCountGrowsWithTheCuts`, `Jam.Slam.ThePatternClosesTheBossTheHeroAndTheWayBack`,
`Jam.Slam.EveryPatternLeavesAReachableSafeSpot`, `Jam.Slam.TheCashStaysClear`, `Jam.Boss.SlamGrowsWithTheCuts`,
`Jam.Bot.WalksOutOfEveryPattern`. Red first on stubs.

# Tickets

One file per ticket. Status: `todo`, `doing`, `done`, `cut`. A ticket is done when its `Jam.` tests are green in
`build_and_test.sh` and the change is committed.

## Architecture in five lines (decided at the start of block A)

- The fight is a **pure simulation**: `FJamFight` (plain data: two fighters, projectiles, hazards, the mechanic
  ledger, the steal state) advanced by `JamFightRules::Step` at a fixed 60 Hz. No world, no actors, flat arena in 2D.
- Everything a fighter does comes in as an **intent** (`FJamIntent`: move, aim, buttons). The player controller, the
  boss brain and the hero bot all write intents, so the hero and the boss run the same mechanic code.
- A **mechanic** is a sim-side component with an owner; a steal is a change of owner in the ledger.
- Folders: `Core` (types, balance, ini loading), `Sim` (rules and the subsystem that hosts the fight), `Game` (glue:
  game mode, controller, demo run), `View` (arena, fighters, projectiles, cameras), `UI`. `Core` and `Sim` never
  include `View`, `UI`, `Audio`. The game mode owns the frame order: input, simulation, views, camera.
- Balance numbers live in one place: `[JamBalance]` in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`.

content.text:
The slam now grows with the cuts: one circle before the first cut, 3 after it, 5 from the second cut on, landing 0.2 s apart from the Publisher outwards. It's committed as `32eeef8`, and all 174 tests pass with no code-check warnings.

- **Always a way out:** a test tries 14,808 placements of the hero and the Publisher over the whole arena, wall included. In every one there is a spot the hero can walk to after 0.3 s to react, without using the dash. A separate step-by-step walk in the test confirms each spot, and every 5-circle slam kept all its circles.
- **Cash:** no circle lands on a cash stack.
- **Bot:** it now walks to the nearest safe spot while circles are on the floor. The old rule only stepped out of the circle it stood in; at the wall it walked into the next one and dropped from 100 to 32 health.
- **Clip:** `Clips/t050_slam_pattern.mp4` (50 s, played by the bot) shows 1 circle, then 3 at 18 s and 28 s, then 5 at 44 s.

**Fight length:** the bot's median went down, from 92 to 83 s, not up. It still wins 60 of 60, and its closest win was at 23 health. The Publisher now stands still until his last circle lands, which gives more openings, and the bot never misreads a pattern. T-038 may add some time, but none of the remaining tickets will bring the bot to 3 to 4 minutes. I wouldn't tune the numbers for the bot: your own time on a full run is the number that matters. The new pattern should cost a person more health than it costs the bot; that isn't measured yet.

**Ideas, not built:**
- Overlapping circles merge into one red patch in the clip. A brighter outline on each circle would show the gaps better; I recommend this one.
- A hand-made shape for each cut: I'd skip it, because the current placement already reads well.

Want a Shipping build to play? It packages in about 3 min, and the smoke test then opens a game window. After that I'll start T-040, the rename.

== package
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Packages the jam project for Win64 into Saved/Packaged/Windows and zips it next to the folder.
3:#   package.sh [--config Development|Shipping] [--name ZipBaseName] [--no-zip]
4:# Builds from the working tree. The editor can stay open: only the game target is compiled.
5:# The submission zip must be named TeamName_GameName: pass it with --name.
34:# Tells builds apart when a tester reports a problem.
== smoke_package
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Starts the packaged game for some seconds and reports what its log says.
3:#   smoke_package.sh [seconds] [map path, e.g. /Game/Maps/L_Main]
4:# Without a map the game opens its default map. A Shipping build writes no log unless it was built with logging:
5:# then only "still running" or "exited by itself" is reported.
13:# A Shipping target is named JamGame-Win64-Shipping.exe.
25:# Git Bash would turn /Game/... into a path under its own install folder.
== itch_push
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Pushes a packaged folder to the itch page pavyny/neon-ronin, channel windows. Key from .env, never printed.
3:#   itch_push.sh <folder> <version>     e.g. itch_push.sh Saved/Packaged/Windows block-d
4:# Needs butler in ~/bin (v15.32.0 installed Sat 14 Nov). Pipe the output through a filter before showing it.

# Session 5 progress report

Written Sat 14 Nov about 16:10 PC clock (UTC+2), mid-session, with the author at the PC. The end-of-session report
will be `Reports/session5_report.md`.

## Clock

- Feature freeze: Sat 22:00 in `HANDOFF.md`; the author moved the cut-off to Sunday morning (chat, 15:50).
- Sunday, unchanged: the video at 18:00, the submission at 20:00, never later than 21:59.

| Ticket | What changed | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T-042 | The Publisher bleeds paper dollars when hit, a big burst on the final blow | clip, tests |
| T-043 | Health 4000, the ball-only stretch after the FINAL NOTE cut from 960 to 120, 7 s on the steal card | bot table |
| T-044 | Parry moved from Q to LMB: the strike parries a shot about to land | tests |
| T-045 | A red arrow at the screen edge points at the Publisher when he is off screen | tests |
| T-046 | The Ultimate shows its lane while ready and fills to the moment it lands | tests |
| T-047 | The edge arrow stops 16 px under the boss health bar | tests |
| T-048 | A retry brings back the hero's health of the last cut (50% if it was 20% or less) | tests |
| T-049 | Every 25 s a hit knocks a glowing cash stack out of him: +25 health, a "ka-ching" | clip, tests |
| T-050 | The slam grows with the cuts: 1, 3, then 5 circles landing 0.2 s apart, always a way out | clip, tests, bot table |

Builds on itch (`pavyny/neon-ronin`, channel `windows`): `session-5a` (#2384201, T-042 to T-046), `session-5b`
(#2384521, T-047 to T-049), `session-5c` with T-050 packaging now.

## State of the game

- 174 `Jam.` tests green (154 at the start of the session), code check without warnings.
- Bot table (60 fights, 20 per steal policy): 60 of 60 won, median 83 s (63 to 172), closest win at 23 health.
- T-050 proof: 14808 slam patterns over the whole arena all leave a spot the hero reaches walking after 0.3 s to
  react; every five-circle pattern kept all five circles.

## Fight length

- The plan's 3 to 4 minutes (`JAM_START_PROMPT.md`) was given up on purpose in T-043: the author asked for a shorter
  fight, and the bot floor went from 120 to 60 s.
- The bot median went 151 s (T-041), 92 s (T-043), 83 s (T-050). T-050 made the bot's fight shorter: the Publisher
  stands until his last circle lands, and the bot never misreads a pattern.
- The bot does not die or retry like a person, and the four steal cards add up to 28 s of reading. A person's full run
  is longer than the bot's; it has not been measured. Recommendation: time one full run by hand on `session-5c` and
  tune only if that is under about 2 minutes.

## Remaining, in the decided order

| # | Ticket | Estimate | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T-040 rename to RONIN: FINAL CUT | 20 min | every visible string; the itch page title is the author's |
| 2 | T-038 the Publisher uses the stolen Parry and Ultimate | 2 to 3 h | boss brain, telegraphs, bot table |
| 3 | T-025/T-026 Meshy models (boss, hero) | about 3 h, risky | needs a spend cap and an answer on rigging; each model shown before import |
| 4 | T-030 a short skippable intro | about 1 h | |
| 5 | T-039 DLSS | unknown | plugin for UE 5.8 not checked; the first to drop |
| Sun | T-032 submission | | itch page, `THIRD_PARTY.md`, tool list, dev log, zip `Pavyny_<GameName>.zip` |

## Known gaps and risks

- Overlapping slam circles merge into one red patch from the top-down camera; a brighter rim per circle would show
  the gaps (proposed, not built).
- Nobody has measured how long a person's fight takes, or how hard the new pattern is for a person.
- Kirill's Drive folder (Q5) has not come; the game plays our ElevenLabs sounds under his names.
- `Jam.Bot.SlashesWhenTheBossIsInReach` was never seen red; `mus_poc_loop.wav` sits twice in `Audio/Eleven`
  (removing one needs a dry run and the author's yes).

## Open for the author

- Meshy: the spend cap, and whether to rig and animate through Meshy or keep the stand-in animations.
- Your time on one full run of `session-5c`.
